evidence.note: Curl health checks across all three HTTP nodes and GET /, confirming the multi-node HTTP surface serves — self-built cross-node checks beyond 'server starts'.
Repeated self-authored python3 heredoc test scripts exercising API endpoints (contents truncated/unseen), indicating reusable programmatic verification across the build.
A node heredoc, almost certainly a WebSocket client test exercising the WS transport.
Active failure injection: identifies a running node via ps, kills it with kill -9, then re-checks health on the surviving nodes — a genuine resilience probe, more than level 5's 'resilience omitted'.
Chromium headless runs driving the SPA, confirming the browser UI is exercised rather than only eyeballed via curl.
Final state/process checks (git status, wc, ps for server/chromium) — light closing verification of running state.

reasoning: The agent self-builds checks spanning HTTP (multi-node), WebSocket (node client), and the browser SPA (chromium), and performs at least one real failure-injection test — SIGKILLing an HTTP node and re-verifying the survivors serve (step 38) — which exceeds level 5's 'resilience thin or omitted'. But I find no visible evidence of the broadcast-component kill, seq-density-under-mixed-writers/resume.gap/cross-node-replay invariants, or an explicit IRC socket session, which are the defining probes of level 8. That places observed behavior between the 5 and 8 anchors at roughly 6; confidence is low because the trajectory is heavily truncated and the contents of the many test scripts are not visible.
